# Papercuts — akr

Small frictions hit while working, logged in the moment (D-027). None of these blocked anything; together they show where the project needs sanding down. Newest first.

- 2026-08-25 [claude] `akr change prepare --staged` reports "code N files" as the whole repository's tracked implementation count, not what the change touches: it read 388 for a change that touched 12, because `Repository::staged_entries` runs `git ls-files --stage`, which lists the entire index rather than what is staged against HEAD. `implementation_digest` wants that whole-tree view and is right to have it, but `SemanticDelta::code` is documented as "implementation files staged" and rendered as this change's contents, so it needs the diff against HEAD instead. Second sighting; misread once as a staging mistake.  `@akr.papercut.akr-change-prepare-staged-reports-code-n-files/1`
- 2026-08-22 [claude] Every AKR-C0nn usage refusal raised through EnvError exits 3 (environment) rather than the exit 2 the diagnostic registry documents for that class — akr evidence add --result nope and --artifact under scratch both do it, so a caller branching on exit status reads a usage error as a broken checkout. The mapping lives in session::EnvError and predates the collated batch.  `@akr.papercut.every-akr-c0nn-usage-refusal-raised-through/1`
- 2026-08-19 [claude-opus-5] Agents write working files to .agent/scratch/ because the protocol tells them to, and nothing ever removes them. Unlike the OS temp directory or target/, that path is inside the repository, is gitignored rather than transient, and no tool, harness or convention prunes it -- so it accumulates across every session until a human hunts it down by hand, reportedly reaching 30GB+ across projects. The guidance makes it worse rather than better: AGENTS.md says scratch notes go there and that 'nobody reviews them and nothing depends on them', which reads as permission to forget them, and scripts/agent-section.md -- the brief actually installed into every agent's global instructions -- does not mention scratch at all, so agents working in other projects never learn the directory is persistent. Spelling has drifted too: the guidance says .agent/scratch/ while this repo tracks a separate .agents/, and several sibling projects now have both.  `@akr.papercut.agents-write-working-files-to-agent-scratch/1`

- 2026-08-18 [claude-opus-5] (claude-code) A subagent spawned with worktree isolation into .claude/worktrees/<id> ran for an hour in a directory that was never a valid git worktree: git resolved its working tree back to the main repo, so `git worktree list` never listed it and `git status` inside it reported the MAIN tree's in-flight changes from other agents as if they were its own. The failure was silent at spawn time and only surfaced when a later resume refused it with work-tree-elsewhere. It cost an hour of a subagent's work and left an orphan directory holding a full cargo target/. Validate the worktree at creation and fail loudly, rather than handing the agent a directory that reads as the parent repo.  `@akr.papercut.a-subagent-spawned-with-worktree-isolation-into/1`
